title: Discovery Loop
summary:
Discovery Loop aims to accelerate scientific and engineering progress by automating the traditionally slow, manual experimental loop. Recognizing that scientific discovery is bottlenecked by repetitive human iterations, their approach utilizes frontier AI models and large-scale computational infrastructure to rapidly propose, run, and learn from thousands of experiments in parallel. This drastically compresses iteration time and improves the quantity and quality of output.

Initially, Discovery Loop will focus on automating machine learning research and engineering, using these capabilities to optimize their own technology. Their long-term mission is to solve any learning loop with measurable outcomes across science and engineering, tackling grand challenges like engineering better medicines and advancing health informatics. They aspire to build AI systems that empower humanity and deliver global technology solutions.

The founding team—Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le, and Oriol Vinyals—are highly cited researchers with decades of close collaboration. They have pioneered massive-scale computing and foundational AI advances, including Google Search, TensorFlow, Gemini, AlphaFold, and large language models. Their unique strength lies in their full-stack depth, spanning chips, hardware, software, ML models, and products. Discovery Loop is building a lean, in-person team to realize this transformative vision, enabling much faster and higher-quality scientific and engineering advancements.
chinese_title: 发现环
chinese_summary:
Discovery Loop 旨在通过自动化传统上缓慢、人工的实验循环，加速科学和工程进步。认识到科学发现受限于重复性的人工迭代，他们的方法利用前沿AI模型和大规模计算基础设施，从而并行快速提出、运行并从数千次实验中学习。这大幅压缩了迭代时间，并提高了产出的数量和质量。

初期，Discovery Loop 将专注于自动化机器学习研究和工程，利用这些能力来优化自身技术。他们的长期使命是解决科学和工程领域中任何具有可衡量成果的学习循环，应对重大挑战，如研发更优药物和推进健康信息学。他们志在构建赋能人类的AI系统，并提供全球技术解决方案。

创始团队——Jeff Dean、Sanjay Ghemawat、Quoc Le和Oriol Vinyals——是备受引用的研究人员，拥有数十年的紧密合作经验。他们开创了大规模计算和基础AI进展，包括Google搜索、TensorFlow、Gemini、AlphaFold和大型语言模型。他们独特的优势在于其全栈深度，涵盖芯片、硬件、软件、机器学习模型和产品。Discovery Loop 正在组建一支精干的线下团队，以实现这一变革性愿景，从而实现更快、更高质量的科学和工程进步。

title: Mario Meets Pareto
summary:
The article "Mario Meets Pareto" by Antoine Mayerowitz applies the economic concept of Pareto efficiency to optimize character and vehicle choices in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. With numerous options for drivers, karts, tires, and gliders, each possessing distinct statistics like speed, acceleration, and handling, players face thousands of build combinations and complex trade-offs.

Mayerowitz introduces Pareto efficiency as a solution to this multi-objective optimization problem. Instead of trying to maximize a single statistic, the Pareto front identifies "efficient" options that are not "dominated." An option is dominated if another build exists that is superior in at least one statistic without being worse in any other. For example, Koopa is shown to be dominated by other drivers who offer better speed or acceleration for the same trade-offs.

The Pareto front comprises all non-dominated choices, objectively filtering out suboptimal options. While it doesn't pinpoint a single "best" build—as the ultimate selection still depends on individual play style and preferences—it significantly narrows down the possibilities to a set of truly optimal trade-offs.

The author emphasizes that this principle extends beyond Mario Kart to various real-world scenarios: seeking a cheap and delicious meal, a well-paid and fulfilling job, a low-risk/high-return investment portfolio, or a high-quality, fast, and cost-efficient AI model. Pareto analysis is particularly valuable when one's utility function (the precise weighting of objectives) is unknown or uncertain, helping to reveal objectively superior alternatives. The article acknowledges simplifying some in-game mechanics for readability.
chinese_title: 马里奥遇上帕累托
chinese_summary:
《马力欧邂逅帕累托》一文作者安托万·梅耶罗维茨运用经济学中的帕累托效率概念，优化了《马力欧卡丁车8豪华版》中的角色和载具选择。由于驾驶员、卡丁车、轮胎和滑翔翼选项众多，每个都拥有速度、加速和操控性等不同的属性，玩家面临数千种组合配置和复杂的权衡取舍。

梅耶罗维茨引入帕累托效率作为解决这个多目标优化问题的方法。帕累托前沿不是试图最大化单一属性，而是识别出未被“支配”的“有效”选项。如果存在另一种配置，至少在一个属性上表现更优，且在其他任何属性上都不差，那么该选项就被认为是“支配”的。例如，库巴被证明受到其他驾驶员的支配，这些驾驶员在相同的权衡取舍下提供更好的速度或加速性能。

帕累托前沿包含所有未被支配的选择，客观地筛选出次优选项。尽管它不能确定一个唯一的“最佳”配置——因为最终选择仍取决于个人游戏风格和偏好——但它将可能性显著缩小到一组真正的最佳权衡取舍。

作者强调，这一原则不仅限于《马力欧卡丁车》，还可应用于各种现实世界场景：寻找物美价廉的餐食、高薪且充实的工作、低风险/高回报的投资组合，或高质量、快速且成本高效的AI模型。当一个人的效用函数（目标的确切权重）未知或不确定时，帕累托分析尤其有价值，它有助于揭示客观上更优的替代方案。该文章承认为了可读性而简化了一些游戏内机制。

title: Changes at Google DeepMind: Demis Hassabis from CEO to Chair, Jeff Dean departs
summary:
Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, announced significant leadership changes at Google DeepMind (GDM) to accelerate AI momentum and focus on Artificial General Intelligence (AGI).

**Demis Hassabis**, previously CEO of Google DeepMind, is transitioning to a new strategic role as **Chair of GDM and Chief Scientist of Alphabet**. In this capacity, he will dedicate his full attention to shaping the future of AGI and science, while also continuing to lead Isomorphic Labs. He will advise GDM teams on models and research, focusing on the broader implications of AGI development.

**Koray Kavukcuoglu**, formerly GDM's Chief Technology Officer and Chief AI Architect, has been promoted to **SVP of Google DeepMind**, reporting directly to Sundar Pichai. He will now oversee Gemini model development, Frontier AI research, and the Gemini app and developer teams, taking over day-to-day operational leadership of GDM.

Additionally, **Jeff Dean**, a Google veteran of 27 years, is departing to co-launch an independent public benefit corporation with Sanjay Ghemawat. This new entity will focus on accelerating discoveries in Machine Learning, science, and engineering, with Google supporting as a founding investor and Cloud partner.

These shifts aim to strengthen Google's position in AI, building on the success of Gemini models (with the app reaching over 950 million monthly users) and ensuring continued leadership across its full AI stack.
chinese_title: 谷歌DeepMind变动：戴密斯·哈萨比斯卸任CEO转任董事长，杰夫·迪恩离职
chinese_summary:
谷歌和Alphabet首席执行官桑达尔·皮查伊宣布谷歌DeepMind (GDM) 进行重大人事调整，旨在加速人工智能发展势头并专注于通用人工智能 (AGI)。

**戴密斯·哈萨比斯**，此前担任谷歌DeepMind首席执行官，将转任新的战略职务，成为**GDM董事长兼Alphabet首席科学家**。在此职位上，他将全身心投入塑造AGI和科学的未来，同时继续领导Isomorphic Labs。他将就模型和研究向GDM团队提供建议，重点关注AGI发展的更广泛影响。

**科雷·卡武库奥卢**，此前担任GDM首席技术官兼首席人工智能架构师，已晋升为**谷歌DeepMind高级副总裁**，直接向桑达尔·皮查伊汇报。他现在将负责Gemini模型开发、前沿AI研究以及Gemini应用和开发者团队，接管GDM的日常运营领导工作。

此外，在谷歌工作27年的资深人士**杰夫·迪恩**将离职，与桑杰·格赫马瓦特共同创立一家独立的公益公司。这家新实体将专注于加速机器学习、科学和工程领域的发现，谷歌将作为创始投资者和云合作伙伴提供支持。

这些变动旨在巩固谷歌在人工智能领域的地位，在Gemini模型（其应用月活跃用户已超过9.5亿）成功的基础上，确保其在整个AI技术栈中的持续领先地位。

title: Crime Pays but Botany Doesn't
summary:
"Crime Pays but Botany Doesn't" offers an enthusiastic guide for self-teaching botany, aiming to demystify the field for beginners. The author encourages learners not to be intimidated by complex terminology, advocating for active online research to understand new words and concepts.

A core principle is the importance of Latin terminology. The article explains that Carl Linnaeus's system provides a universal, precise nomenclature, essential because common names are often ambiguous. Proper scientific naming—genus capitalized, species lowercase, both italicized—is presented as fundamental, with incorrect formatting signaling a lack of knowledge. Taxonomy itself is celebrated as a "fucking cool" method for grouping organisms by evolutionary relatedness, enabling botanists to identify unfamiliar plants based on shared traits.

For in-depth study, two primary textbooks are recommended: *Plant Systematics* by Michael Simpson, a seminal work on plant evolution, morphology, and synapomorphies; and *Raven's Biology of Plants*, which covers foundational biology, evolutionary concepts, and charismatic plant species.

Acknowledging the cost of self-education, the guide also lists numerous additional texts on various botanical topics. Importantly, it suggests utilizing resources like Libgen and Sci-hub for accessing PDF versions of textbooks, promoting the use of affordable Android tablets to democratize access to extensive botanical knowledge.
chinese_title: 犯罪赚钱，植物学不赚钱
chinese_summary:
《犯罪有报，植物学无》（"Crime Pays but Botany Doesn't"）是一本热情的植物学自学指南，旨在为初学者揭开其神秘面纱。作者鼓励学习者不要被复杂的术语吓倒，主张积极在线研究以理解新词和概念。

一个核心原则是拉丁语术语的重要性。文章解释说，卡尔·林奈的系统提供了一种通用、精确的命名法，这至关重要，因为俗名往往模棱两可。正确的科学命名——属名首字母大写，种名小写，二者均斜体——被认为是基础，格式不正确则表明缺乏知识。分类学本身被誉为一种“真是他妈的酷”的方法，它通过进化亲缘关系对生物进行分组，使植物学家能够根据共同特征识别不熟悉的植物。

为了深入学习，推荐了两本主要教科书：迈克尔·辛普森（Michael Simpson）的《植物系统学》（*Plant Systematics*），这是一部关于植物进化、形态学和共有衍征的开创性著作；以及《雷文植物生物学》（*Raven's Biology of Plants*），涵盖了基础生物学、进化概念和富有魅力的植物物种。

考虑到自学的成本，该指南还列出了大量关于各种植物学主题的补充读物。重要的是，它建议利用Libgen和Sci-hub等资源获取教科书的PDF版本，并提倡使用经济实惠的安卓平板电脑，以普及广泛的植物学知识。

title: Cloudflare OS: an open platform for agents, apps, and work
summary:
Cloudflare OS is an open platform designed to empower every person within an organization with AI agents and workspaces tailored to their company's unique context, systems, and mission. It extends AI's leverage beyond code, enabling agents to understand company procedures, access internal systems, and perform diverse work, from document creation to building applications.

The platform features an agent workspace grounded in curated company context and skills, an isolated runtime for code execution, a robust security and governance framework, and a platform for personal, modifiable apps. Users can interact conversationally to research topics, generate dynamic documents, spreadsheets, and presentations connected to live data, create collaborative apps, and automate workflows.

A key differentiator is its security model. Agents start with no access, and "Gatekeepers" mediate granular access to external services, enforcing policies, masking sensitive fields, and auditing data observations. This ensures that sharing outputs or apps doesn't inadvertently expose restricted information, as policy follows observed data.

Apps built within Cloudflare OS are full-stack, powered by Cloudflare Workers, allowing for real-time collaboration or sharing as "blueprints" for independent copies. The platform is model-agnostic, using Cloudflare AI Gateway for cost control and attribution. Open-sourced and customizable, Cloudflare OS allows organizations to integrate their own systems, policies, and UI, with partners available for deployment and customization. Future plans include a managed product and chat tool integrations.
chinese_title: Cloudflare OS：一个面向代理、应用和业务的开放平台
chinese_summary:
Cloudflare OS是一个开放平台，旨在通过AI代理和工作区赋能组织内的每个人，这些代理和工作区根据公司独特的背景、系统和使命量身定制。它将AI的影响力从代码扩展开来，使代理能够理解公司流程、访问内部系统，并执行从文档创建到应用程序构建等各种工作。

该平台具有基于精选公司背景和技能的代理工作区、用于代码执行的隔离运行时、强大的安全和治理框架，以及一个用于个人可修改应用程序的平台。用户可以通过对话方式进行交互，以研究主题、生成连接到实时数据的动态文档、电子表格和演示文稿、创建协作应用程序以及自动化工作流程。

其安全模型是一个关键区别。代理初始不具备任何访问权限，“守门人”调解对外部服务的精细访问，执行策略、屏蔽敏感字段并审计数据观察。这确保了共享输出或应用程序不会无意中暴露受限信息，因为策略会跟随被观察到的数据。

在Cloudflare OS中构建的应用程序是全栈的，由Cloudflare Workers提供支持，允许实时协作或作为独立副本的“蓝图”进行共享。该平台与模型无关，使用Cloudflare AI Gateway进行成本控制和归因。Cloudflare OS是开源且可定制的，允许组织集成自己的系统、策略和UI，并有合作伙伴提供部署和定制服务。未来的计划包括托管产品和聊天工具集成。

title: Zed DeltaDB
summary:
Zed DeltaDB is an early access version control system that records development work as it unfolds, uniquely linking every change to the "agent conversation" that shaped it. It captures every operation between commits, assigning each a stable identity, allowing users to rewind to any specific edit in the code's evolution and easily trace code changes back to their conversational origins.

A key feature is its virtualized worktree, which makes creating new "agent branches" effectively free, even from a mid-run point in history. This enables a new mode of collaboration where teammates can join ongoing work, interact with the agent responsible for changes, and annotate in real-time without waiting for commits or pushes. Designed for integration with the Zed editor, DeltaDB aims to streamline the coding process. Users are invited to download or clone the source to try it.
chinese_title: 泽德 德尔塔数据库
chinese_summary:
Zed DeltaDB 是一个抢先体验版版本控制系统，它记录开发工作的实时进展，独特地将每个更改与其形成过程中的“代理对话”关联起来。它捕获提交之间的每一次操作，为每一次操作分配一个稳定的标识，允许用户回溯到代码演进过程中的任何特定编辑，并轻松地将代码更改追溯到其对话源头。

一个关键特性是它的虚拟化工作树，这使得创建新的“代理分支”几乎没有成本，甚至可以从历史进程中的任意中间节点开始。这开启了一种新的协作模式，团队成员可以加入正在进行的工作，与负责更改的代理进行交互，并进行实时注释，而无需等待提交或推送。DeltaDB 专为与 Zed 编辑器集成而设计，旨在简化编码过程。欢迎用户下载或克隆源代码进行试用。

title: Civilian plane crash in New Mexico tied to military GPS blocking
summary:
A medevac plane crashed in New Mexico this May, killing four, during a US military GPS jamming exercise at White Sands Missile Range. This marked the first civilian plane crash in the US attributed to GPS jamming. The twin-engine Beechcraft King Air, carrying an inexperienced pilot and co-pilot, lost GPS eight minutes after takeoff from Roswell while en route to Ruidoso. Forced to use older, less familiar navigation, the crew became disoriented.

The military's "NAVFEST" exercise, intended for electronic warfare training, jammed GPS signals up to 400 miles away, despite FAA warnings. Air traffic control was overwhelmed, assisting multiple aircraft experiencing GPS loss. After initially losing GPS and overshooting their landing pattern, the King Air pilots opted for a visual approach in the dark, moonless night. Unaware of the 10,000-foot Capitan Mountains directly in their path, they flew straight into the rising terrain.

This incident underscores a growing global risk from expanding drone and electronic warfare, which frequently causes GPS disruptions for civilian aviation worldwide. Experts warn that routine GPS interference undermines safety, eroding pilot trust in instruments. Other US incidents, like Secret Service jamming near Reagan Airport and CBP drone operations in West Texas, exemplify this trend. The aviation industry is criticized for its slow adaptation, with suggestions that further "catastrophes" may be needed to drive essential safety changes in this increasingly contested airspace.
chinese_title: 新墨西哥州民航坠机关联军事GPS屏蔽
chinese_summary:
今年五月，一架医疗救援飞机在新墨西哥州坠毁，造成四人死亡，当时美军正在白沙导弹靶场进行GPS干扰演习。这标志着美国首次有民用飞机坠毁被归咎于GPS干扰。这架双引擎比奇空中国王飞机，载有一名经验不足的飞行员和副驾驶，从罗斯威尔起飞八分钟后，在前往鲁伊多索的途中失去GPS信号。机组人员被迫使用老旧且不熟悉的导航方式，因此迷失了方向。

尽管美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）发出了警告，军方的“NAVFEST”演习（旨在进行电子战训练）仍干扰了最远达400英里范围内的GPS信号。空中交通管制部门不堪重负，为多架遭遇GPS信号丢失的飞机提供协助。在最初失去GPS并飞越着陆模式后，空中国王飞机的飞行员选择在漆黑无月的夜晚进行目视进近。他们没有意识到正前方有10,000英尺高的卡皮坦山脉，径直飞入了正在上升的地形。

此次事件凸显了日益增长的全球风险，即无人机和电子战的扩张经常导致全球民用航空的GPS中断。专家警告称，日常的GPS干扰会损害飞行安全，侵蚀飞行员对仪器的信任。美国其他事件，例如特勤局在里根机场附近的干扰以及美国海关与边境保护局（CBP）在西德克萨斯州的无人机操作，都印证了这一趋势。航空业因其缓慢的适应速度而受到批评，有人建议，可能需要更多的“灾难”才能推动在这个日益竞争的空域中实现必要的安全变革。
